title: Envelope
description: One message on the wire. A reply carries the `id` of the request it answers.

oneOf.description: An element picked in Chrome, from the extension's host to a core that offers element.pick.
What a run reported, from the core to clients that have the capability `run.stream`.

A change to a workspace, from the server to clients that have the capability
`workspace.feed`.
A log record from a client, sent only to a peer that offers `log.forward`.
What a person asks of a chat's agent, from a client to a core that offers `chat.send`.

A committed event of a chat, from the core to a client that subscribed under
`chat.events`.
A question about a chat's log, from a client to a core that offers `chat.events`.

The core's answer to a [`ChatQuery`], or its word that the client missed events, to a
client that has `chat.events`.
A question about a chat's changes, from a client to a core that offers `diff.view`.

The core's answer to a [`DiffQuery`], one changed file at a time, to a client that has
`diff.view`.

A question about what a machine keeps for a workspace, from a client to a core that
offers `machine.settings`.

A change to what a machine keeps for a workspace, from a client to a core that offers
`machine.settings`.

The core's answer to a [`MachineSettingsQuery`] or a [`MachineSettingsCommand`], to a
client that has `machine.settings`.

A sign-in terminal's sealed input, from a browser through the server to a core that
offers `terminal.sign_in`; the server relays it only if it offers `terminal.relay`.

A sign-in terminal's sealed output, from a core that offers `terminal.sign_in` through
the server to the browser that opened it.

A question about a chat's worktree, from a client to a core that offers
`worktree.manage`.

What a person asks of a chat's worktree, from a client to a core that offers
`worktree.manage`.

The core's answer to a [`WorktreeQuery`] or a [`WorktreeCommand`], to a client that has
`worktree.manage`.

AccessLevel.description: What a workspace's agents may do on one machine, chosen by the machine's owner.

oneOf.description: No agent runs.
Agents ask a person before each change.
Agents change things without asking; destructive operations still ask.

AccountId.description: A person's account on the server, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

AccountSignInFinish.description:
Trades the one-time code sent to `email`, and the challenge its [`SignInStarted`] gave,
for an [`AccountSignedIn`].

AccountSignInStart.description:
Asks the server to send a one-time code to `email`, if that person may sign in. The
answer, a [`SignInStarted`], is the same either way.

AccountSignedIn.description:
The signed-in account. `token`, sent as a bearer token, is only in the answer to an
[`AccountSignInFinish`], for clients that keep no cookie.

oneOf.description: A member's own, under their sign-in.
The workspace's shared agent, under the workspace's own credential.

AgentRef.description: An agent as people know it.

machine.description:
What the machine it runs on is called, which the server stamps from its own record of
the core that sent the status and never takes from the core; left out when not known.

AgentSession.description: An agent's own id for a conversation, a lowercase UUID, which resumes it later.

App.description: A program, such as `weacon-core`, and the exact build it is.

Asker.description:
Who asked for a command, stamped by the server on what it relays to a machine and never
taken from a client. The core acts only when `account` is its owner's, and records only
`member`.

Author.description: Who made a change, such as one to a task.

oneOf.description: An agent, named by the member it answers to, and by which agent it is when known.

BuildTarget.description: A Rust target a release is built for, such as `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`.

Bytes.description:
Bytes that travel as lowercase hex, at most [`NOISE_MAX`] of them. Its `Debug` shows only
how many, since they are sealed or terminal content.

Capability.description:
A feature a peer supports, such as `chat.send`, named like a [`Code`]. A peer keeps the ones
it doesn't know, so a newer peer's list still parses.

ChallengeId.description:
One sign-in request, which its code and its tries belong to; 1–64 ASCII letters,
digits, `-` or `_`.

oneOf.description:
Starts or queues a turn. Only a chat's first prompt has `repo` and `machine`, one of the
sender's; the server drops `machine` before relaying.
Answers a permission prompt of one of the chat's runs.
Stops the turn that is running.

The client missed events and its subscription is over: fetch a snapshot, then subscribe
after its `seq`.

The chat as of `seq`: its runs, where in the log the permission prompts still waiting
are, and its latest events, as many as fit one frame. A `window` fetches a prompt that
isn't among them.

ChatCommand.description: The core answers with receipts under `request`.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the command to a machine.

ChatEntry.description: An event and its place in its chat's log: `seq` starts at 1 and grows by one.

oneOf.description: A person's prompt, accepted under `request`, with the repository it fixed, if any.
Where a chat command stands; written once per state.

ChatId.description: A chat in a workspace, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

ChatList.description:
A workspace's chats, from the server, to clients that have the capability
`workspace.chats`.

ChatQuery.description: The answer is a [`ChatAnswer`], or for `subscribe` the [`ChatUpdate`]s themselves.

oneOf.description: Every event after `after`, then each new one as it is committed.

The latest events before `before`: at most `limit`, and fewer when they wouldn't fit
one frame.

ChatState.description: What can still happen to a chat.

oneOf.description: Its owner can prompt it.
Its workspace has no room for more of its events, so it takes no prompts until it has.
Its machine was unpaired, or no longer has its log: it can be read, never prompted.

ChatSummary.description:
A chat in a [`ChatList`]: `machine` is a name, never an id, and `updated_at` is when its
latest turn began or ended, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

ChatUpdate.description: Text deltas are never committed; they arrive only as run updates.

ClientLog.description:
A log record from a client that has no log of its own, such as the web app: an event name and
typed ids. The receiver logs only events it knows, so no other text reaches its log.

Code.description:
A dotted code such as `store.full`: two or more lowercase words joined by dots. It names
errors, and capabilities too.

Commit.description: A full git commit id: 40 lowercase hex digits.

CommitId.description: A git commit, as 40 or 64 lowercase hex digits.

DiffAnswer.description: From the core to a client that has `diff.view`, in answer to a [`DiffQuery`].

oneOf.description:
One of the `files` changed files, which arrive one answer each, in order; `files` is at
least 1 and the same in every answer to one query.
Nothing changed.
No hunks when only the file's mode changed.
The file's changes wouldn't fit one frame.

path.description: Where the file is now, or was when it was removed, relative to the worktree.

DiffLine.description: One line without its `\n`, so a `\r` before it stays in `text`.

no_newline.description: The file's last line, when it has no `\n`.

DiffQuery.description:
From a client to a core that offers `diff.view`. Each answer is a [`DiffAnswer`] that echoes
`request`.

oneOf.description: Every file the chat's agents changed in its worktree.

DocAnchors.description: A pin for each anchor a doc links to, all computed at `commit`.

DocContent.description:
What one revision of a doc says: its title, its Markdown, and the anchors it links to,
unless it links to none.

DocHistory.description: A doc's revisions, newest first, from the server.

DocId.description: A doc in a workspace, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

DocList.description: A workspace's docs, from the server.

DocPin.description:
An anchor a doc links to, with the fingerprint the code had at the revision's commit:
`sym:weacon_protocol::frame::encode_line#0123456789abcdef`, in printable ASCII. The core
computes both; the server only checks their shape.

DocRecord.description:
A doc at one revision; `version` rises with each revision. The server sends it to clients
that have the capability `workspace.docs`.

DocRevise.description:
Asks the server for a new revision of a doc that the client read at `version`; the server
refuses when the doc has changed since. The answer is its [`DocRecord`].

DocRevision.description:
Who made one revision of a doc, who accepted it, and when, in seconds since the Unix
epoch.

DocSummary.description: A doc in a [`DocList`], without its body.

DownloadUrl.description:
An `https://` address of printable ASCII, at most 2,048 bytes, with a plain host name and
optionally a port: no user name or password.

retryable.description: Whether the same request can succeed if sent again later.

Hello.description: The first message on every connection, from the side that connects.

Hunk.description:
A run of changed lines and their context. Lines count from 1; the start of a side with no
lines, as the old side of an added file, is 0.

oneOf.description: Very noisy.
Developer detail.
Lifecycle.
Failed and handled.
A person needs to look.
About to exit.

LogEvent.description:
What happened, such as `run started`: one to four words of lowercase letters or `_`, one
space apart, at most 40 bytes; no digits, so ids and secrets can't be spelt in it.

MachineId.description: A machine paired with an account, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

MachineKey.description:
A machine's public X25519 key, the static key of its sealed channels, as 64 lowercase hex
digits. A browser pins it when the person confirms the pairing.

MachineList.description: The machines paired with the signed-in account.

MachineName.description:
What a machine is called: 1–64 characters, none of them control or bidirectional
formatting characters, so it shows the same wherever it is shown.

MachineOs.description: The operating system a machine runs.

MachineSettings.description: What a machine keeps for one workspace, and whether it sends error reports.

reports.description: The owner's answer to error reports; absent until they give one, when none are sent.

sign_ins.description: Each agent the core runs, signed in or not with the workspace's own config folder.

team.description: Whether other people are in the workspace.

oneOf.description: Whether the machine sends error reports; for the whole machine, not one workspace.

What `workspace`'s agents may do on the machine, and whether other people are in it;
`team` is kept as it was when left out.

MachineSettingsAnswer.description:
From the core to a client that has `machine.settings`, in answer to a
[`MachineSettingsQuery`] or a [`MachineSettingsCommand`].

MachineSettingsCommand.description:
From the owner of `machine` to its core, which offers `machine.settings`: changes what the
machine keeps for `workspace`. The server relays it only from the machine's owner, and the
core acts only when `by` is its owner; the answer is a [`MachineSettingsAnswer`] that echoes
`request` and holds the settings after the change.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the message to a machine.

MachineSettingsQuery.description:
From the owner of `machine` to its core, which offers `machine.settings`: what the machine
keeps for `workspace`. The server relays it only from the machine's owner, and the core
answers only when `by` is its owner; the answer is a [`MachineSettingsAnswer`] that echoes
`request`.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the message to a machine.

oneOf.description: The settings as they are now.

MachineSummary.description:
A machine paired with the signed-in account, at `paired_at`, in seconds since the Unix
epoch.

MemberId.description: A member of a workspace, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

Outcome.description:
Where an accepted command stands. It ends `completed`, `interrupted`, `failed` or `unknown`.
`unknown` means it may or may not have run, as when a restart cut it off; the client must not
send it again under a new id.

PairClaim.description:
From the core that started `pairing`: whether the person has confirmed it yet. The answer
is a [`PairClaimed`].

oneOf.description: Not confirmed yet: claim again later.

Paired with `owner`'s account. The core proves itself with `token`, sent as a bearer
token, which the server hands out only once.

PairConfirm.description:
From the web app, signed in: pairs the machine waiting under `code` with the signed-in
account. The answer is its [`MachineSummary`].

PairLookup.description:
From the web app, signed in: the machine waiting under `code`. The answer is a
[`PairPending`].

PairPending.description: A machine waiting to be paired, for the person to check against what its terminal shows.

PairStart.description:
From a core to the server, unauthenticated: starts pairing the machine. The answer is a
[`PairStarted`]; the server refuses an `os` it doesn't know.

PairStarted.description:
The answer to a [`PairStart`]: the single-use `code` the person enters in the web app, and
the `secret` only the core that started may claim the machine with, until `expires_at`, in
seconds since the Unix epoch.

PairingId.description:
One pairing of a machine, from its start to its claim; 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-`
or `_`.

Pick.description:
An element someone picked on a local web page, sent to the core for a chat. The sender cuts
the HTML short and shrinks the screenshot so the message fits in one frame.

screenshot_png.description:
What the element looked like: a PNG, base64-encoded. None when the page couldn't be
captured.

selector.description: A CSS selector that finds the element on the page.

Receipt.description: The daemon's word on a command, sent when it is accepted and again when it ends.

ReleaseBuild.description: One target's binary in a release.

ReleaseManifest.description: A release, as its signed manifest describes it; a core reads it to update itself.

builds.description: At most one for each target.

published_at.description:
When the release was signed, in seconds since the Unix epoch, so a core can tell a
manifest that is being held back from the newest one.

ReleaseVersion.description: A release's `major.minor.patch`, ordered by its numbers.

RepoId.description:
A git repository the owner registered for a workspace on their machine, 1–64 ASCII
letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

RequestId.description:
A command's id, chosen by the client and kept across reconnects and retries. Sending the
same id again returns the first receipt instead of repeating the work; the same id with
different content is refused with the error `request.conflict`.

RunEvent.description: What an agent's run reports, in order. Each turn ends with `finished`.

oneOf.description: The agent's conversation, to resume it later.
More of the text block being written; the [`RunEvent::Text`] that follows replaces it.
The agent asks to use a tool and waits for a [`PermissionAnswer`].
The agent no longer waits for the answer to `prompt`.
Ends the turn and withdraws any prompt still waiting.

RunId.description:
The core's id for one run of an agent process, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.
Prompts carry it, so an answer only ever reaches the run that asked.

oneOf.description: The agent process is starting.
On a turn.
On a turn, waiting for a person to answer a permission prompt.
Between turns, with its process alive.
Its process was stopped; the next prompt resumes the same agent session in a new run.
Over for good.

RunStatus.description: Where a run stands, as its chat's log records it.

agent.description: Who runs it; left out when not known.

RunUpdate.description: One event of the run `run`, in the order the run reported it.

Sha256.description: A SHA-256 digest: 64 lowercase hex digits.

SignInFinish.description:
Trades the one-time code sent to `email` for a [`SignedIn`]. `challenge` is the one its
[`SignInStarted`] gave; a server that hands out challenges refuses a finish without one.

SignInStart.description:
Sign-in to one workspace, which [`AccountSignInStart`] replaces: asks the server to send
a one-time code to `email`, if it is a member of `workspace`. The answer, a [`SignInStarted`], is the same either way.

SignInStarted.description:
The answer to a [`SignInStart`], for members and strangers alike: the challenge to finish
it with.

SignInState.description: Only whether an agent is signed in: never its credentials.

oneOf.description: The vendor's tool didn't say.

SignedIn.description: A signed-in member and the session token that proves it, sent as a bearer token.

TaskChange.description:
Asks the server to change a task that the client read at `version`; the server refuses
when the task has changed since. The answer is its [`TaskRecord`].

TaskCreate.description:
Asks the server for a new task, placed in front of `before`, or last without one. The
answer is its [`TaskRecord`].

TaskEditBody.description: One edit to a task, inside a [`TaskChange`].

oneOf.description: Places the task in front of `before`, or last without one.

TaskId.description: A task in a workspace, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

TaskList.description: A workspace's tasks in their order, from the server.

TaskRecord.description:
A task as it travels: `order` is its order key and `version` rises with each change. The
server sends it to clients that have the capability `workspace.tasks`.

TaskStatus.description: How far along a task is.

oneOf.description:
Runs `agent`'s login, with the first handshake message, whose payload is a
[`TerminalInput::Resize`].
A sealed [`TerminalInput`].
Ends the login, if it still runs.

TerminalCommand.description:
From the owner of `machine`'s browser to its core, which offers `terminal.sign_in`. The
server relays it only from the machine's owner, and the core acts only when `by` is its
owner and refuses a terminal id it has already seen.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the message to a machine.

oneOf.description: The second handshake message, with an empty payload.
A sealed [`TerminalOutput`].
The terminal is gone; nothing more comes. `code` says why, unless it ended as asked.

TerminalId.description:
One sign-in terminal, chosen by the browser that opens it; 1–64 ASCII letters, digits,
`-` or `_`.

TerminalInput.description: From the browser to the core, only inside the seal.

oneOf.description: What the person typed or pasted.
The terminal's size in characters.

TerminalOutput.description: From the core to the browser, only inside the seal.

oneOf.description: What the login printed.
The login ended, and then the vendor's status command said this.

TerminalUpdate.description:
From a core that offers `terminal.sign_in`, through the server, to the browser that opened
`terminal`.

Welcome.description: The answer to a [`Hello`] that speaks the same protocol.

oneOf.description: A member opened the workspace for the first time.

A task was made, at version 1, or changed. Only for clients that have the capability
`workspace.tasks`, which read the tasks again to see what it now is.

A doc was made, at version 1, or revised. Only for clients that have the capability
`workspace.docs`, which read the doc again to see what it now says.

A chat was made, or its title, state or latest turn changed. Only for clients that have
the capability `workspace.chats`, which read the chats again.

WorkspaceCreate.description:
Asks the server for a new workspace, which the asker owns. The answer is its
[`WorkspaceSummary`].

WorkspaceId.description: A workspace on the server, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

WorkspaceList.description: The workspaces the signed-in account is a member of.

WorkspaceRole.description: What a member may do in a workspace.

oneOf.description: Made the workspace.
Was added to it.

WorkspaceSummary.description: A workspace as one of its members sees it, with their `role` in it.

WorkspaceUpdate.description:
One change to `workspace`. `seq` grows strictly within a workspace, and a feed opened with
`since=N` sends every change after `N`.

oneOf.description: Moves the worktree to the Trash; its branch stays.
Brings the worktree back from the Trash to where it was.
Pushes the chat's branch and opens a draft pull request from it.

WorktreeAnswer.description:
From the core to a client that has `worktree.manage`, in answer to a [`WorktreeQuery`] or a
[`WorktreeCommand`].

oneOf.description:
Where the worktree stands, in the Trash or not. A chat with no worktree yet gets the
error `worktree.none`.
The branch was pushed and a draft pull request opened at `url`.

The branch was pushed, but no pull request could be opened from here; `url` is the
page where the person can open one.

WorktreeCommand.description:
From a client to a core that offers `worktree.manage`: what a person asks of a chat's
worktree. The core acts only for someone who may act on the chat, and a client asks the
person before `remove`, whatever the access level. The answer is a [`WorktreeAnswer`] that
echoes `request`: the worktree's state after `remove` or `restore`, which a repeated one
answers too.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the command to a machine.

WorktreeQuery.description:
From a client to a core that offers `worktree.manage`: a question about a chat's worktree.
The answer is a [`WorktreeAnswer`] that echoes `request`.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the query to a machine.

oneOf.description: Whether the worktree is in the Trash, and what removing it would set aside.
